Report DescriptionTHIS IS A POTENTIAL RELEASE OF LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES DUE TO A DERAILMENT OF 23 RAIL CARS. CANADIAN NATIONAL (CN) TRAIN M-3063125 DERAILED AT MILE POINT 8.0 OF PELLETIER SUBDIVISION IN EDMUNDSTON, NB. 23 RAIL CARS DERAILED INCLUDING 4 LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES LOADS AND 5 LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES RESIDUE. THE TRAIN WAS TRAVELING AT 46 MILES PER HOUR HEADING EAST BOUND AT THE TIME OF THE DERAILMENT. LOCAL POLICE IS ON SITE. 3 CROSSINGS ARE BLOCKED BY THE DERAILMENT. THERE IS NO LEAK , NO INJURIES, NO EXPOSURES OR FIRE. THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE ASSISTANCE PLAN (ERAP) WILL BE IMPLEMENTED AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE TEAMS WILL BE GOING ON SITE, AS WELL AS CN PERSONNEL (ESTIMATED TIME OF ARRIVAL IS FROM 5 HOURS TO MORE THAN 12 HOURS FOR THE VARIOUS TEAMS). INCIDENT IS IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE CANADA-US INTERNATIONAL BOARDER AND CLOSE TO A SMALL TRIBUTARY TO THE ST. JOHN RIVER.

THE TRAIN WAS TRAVELING AT 46 MILES PER HOUR HEADING EAST BOUND AT THE TIME OF THE DERAILMENT. LOCAL POLICE IS ON SITE. 3 CROSSINGS ARE BLOCKED BY THE DERAILMENT. THERE IS NO LEAK , NO INJURIES, NO EXPOSURES OR FIRE. THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE ASSISTANCE PLAN (ERAP) WILL BE IMPLEMENTED AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE TEAMS WILL BE GOING ON SITE, AS WELL AS CN PERSONNEL (ESTIMATED TIME OF ARRIVAL IS FROM 5 HOURS TO MORE THAN 12 HOURS FOR THE VARIOUS TEAMS). INCIDENT IS IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE CANADA-US INTERNATIONAL BOARDER AND CLOSE TO A SMALL TRIBUTARY TO THE ST. JOHN RIVER.

THE VESSEL ENTER THE BAY AND RAN AGROUND ON A SAND BAR AT 70°51.41N, 158°41.44W. TOTAL CAPACITY FOR VESSEL IS 211 GALLONS OF DIESEL FUEL. VESSEL WAS NOT AT TOTAL CAPACITY AT THE TIME OF INCIDENT.

properties.title: NRC Report: Hydraulic Oil near Point Of Rocks, WY
properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 984500 - Medium Affected: SOIL - Suspected Responsible Party: BLACK BUTTE COAL
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 984500
Incident Time: 2011-07-30 03:00:00
Nearest City: Point Of Rocks, WY
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: HYDRAULIC OIL
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: BLACK BUTTE COAL
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 60 gallons
A CAT D-11 BULLDOZER WAS PERFORMING RECLAMATION IN PIT 24 OF THE LEUCITE HILLS MINE WHEN A HYDRAULIC LINE ON THE BULLDOZER FAILED, ALLOWING 60 GALLONS OF HYDRAULIC FLUID TO SPILL ON THE GROUND. AN IMPOUNDMENT LOCATED DOWN THE DRAINAGE FROM THE BULLDOZER CATCHES ALL OF THE RUNOFF IN THE DRAINAGE, THEREFORE THERE WAS NO POTENTIAL FOR THE SPILL MATERIAL TO RELEASE TO A BODY OF WATER. ONCE THE SPILL OCCURRED THE BULLDOZER WAS SHUT DOWN. THE HYDRAULIC OIL WAS THEN SOAKED UP WITH ABSORBANT MATERIAL, AND ALL CONTAMINATED SOIL WAS TAKEN TO THE PERMITTED LANDFARM ON SITE.

THE NATURE OF THE POINT SOURCE COULD NOT BE DETERMINED, BUT IT WAS LOCATED 11 NM SE OF BAYOU BLANC IN MARSH IS. THE ANOMALY WAS JAGGED WITH SHARP TURNS NEAR THE SOURCE AND WAS CONTINUOUS FOR 9.5 NM AND BROKEN FOR AN ADDITIONAL 4.2 NM WHERE THE ANOMALY EXTENDED FROM NE TO SW. THE ANOMALY EXISTED IN NEAR SHORE WATERS AMIDST TIGHTLY PACKED BATHYMETRIC LINES IN WATERS LADEN WITH SEDIMENTS AS A RESULT OF SUBSTANTIAL RUNOFF.

Report DescriptionTHE CALLER STATED THAT DURING SWA FLIGHT 1952 (SAN TO SMF) A PASSENGER"S VAPE DEVICE STARTED HEATING UP IN HIS PACKET WHILE HE WAS IN THE LAVATORY. THE PASSENGER TOOK THE DEVICE OUT OF HIS POCKET AND IT BEGAN TO SMOKE AND EVENTUALLY CAUGHT FIRE. THE DEVICE WAS RAN UNDER WATER TO EXTINGUISH THE FIRE AND THEN THROWN AWAY. WHEN THE PASSENGER LEFT THE LAVATORY HE INFORMED THE FLIGHT ATTENDANT WHO RETRIEVED THE DEVICE AND PLACED IT IN A CONTAINMENT BAG. ONCE THE FLIGHT LANDED AT SMF THE DEVICE WAS RELINQUISHED TO THE FIRE DEPARTMENT WHO DISPOSED OF THE ITEM. THERE WERE NO INJURIES, FATALITIES, OR DIVERSIONS IN CONNECTION TO THIS INCIDENT.
